## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.22 — About screen, attribution, and a real icon

### The app finally has its own icon

It had been shipping a stock Android system drawable (`ic_menu_compass`). No
store accepts that, and those drawables are not stable API — they are whatever
the manufacturer's framework happens to contain.

The replacement is a bulb over three fanning bars: one source driving several
channels, which is what the app does and what "mux" means. It is a vector, so
it costs about a kilobyte instead of five PNGs, and it doubles as the Android
13+ themed icon that recolours to your wallpaper.

### Settings → About

Version, licence, and a link to the source. Plus the full text of every
third-party licence, **served from inside the app** rather than linked — a
phone with no internet can still show it, which is rather the point for an app
that runs entirely on your own network.

That list is generated from the modules actually linked into the build, and CI
fails if a dependency is added without its attribution, or arrives under a
licence incompatible with GPL-3.

### Android reported the wrong version

The About screen and every diagnostics report from a phone said the version was
"android" — which answers a different question from the one being asked. It now
reports the build you actually installed.

### Store listing prepared

Listing text in English and Polish is in the repository, ready for
IzzyOnDroid — an F-Droid-compatible repository that takes the APK already built
here. Screenshots still to come.
